docs.title: Welcome to Easy IDP
docs.text:
Easy IDP is a GitOps-native Internal Developer Platform that enables developers to create and execute workflows through guided forms.

Quick Start

New to Easy IDP? Start with our Installation Guide or jump straight to the Quickstart.

docs.title: What is Easy IDP?
docs.text: Easy IDP simplifies platform engineering by providing a self-service portal for common developer workflows. Instead of writing scripts or managing complex CI/CD pipelines, developers fill out simple forms that execute predefined workflows.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
✨ GitOps-First Configuration as code with Git version control, code review, and rollback capabilities.

🔄 Workflow Management Create workflows with dynamic forms - no complex YAML or scripting required.

🔑 Credential Management Secure storage and templating of sensitive credentials with automatic secret redaction.

🌐 Global Variables Centralized configuration values accessible across all workflows.

⚡ Action Primitives Powerful, composable actions: HTTP requests, shell commands, templates, and flow control.

📊 Real-time Execution Step-by-step workflow execution with live status updates and detailed logging.

docs.title: Why Easy IDP?
docs.text:
Traditional internal developer platforms are complex and require significant infrastructure:

  • ❌ Kubernetes clusters
  • ❌ Multiple services and dependencies
  • ❌ Weeks of setup time
  • ❌ Dedicated platform engineering team

Easy IDP takes a different approach:

  • ✅ Single Docker container
  • ✅ No Kubernetes required
  • ✅ Set up in minutes
  • ✅ Maintainable by small teams

docs.title: Service Deployment
docs.text: Deploy new services with pre-configured workflows that handle repository creation, CI/CD setup, and initial deployment.

docs.title: Infrastructure Provisioning
docs.text: Provision databases, DNS records, SSL certificates, and other infrastructure through simple forms.

docs.title: Developer Onboarding
docs.text: Create workflows that set up developer environments, grant access, and configure tools automatically.

docs.title: Compliance & Governance
docs.text: Enforce policies and standards through workflow templates with built-in validation.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Easy IDP follows a simple, straightforward architecture:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Platform Config Repository (Git)       │
│  ├── globals.json                       │
│  ├── workflows/                         │
│  └── catalog/                           │
└─────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
              │
              │ GitOps Sync (Pull-based)
              │
              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Easy IDP Application                   │
│  ├── Web UI (Forms)                     │
│  ├── Workflow Engine                    │
│  ├── Credential Store                   │
│  └── Execution Logs                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Easy IDP can be installed in multiple ways depending on your environment and preferences.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker and Docker Compose (for containerized deployment)
  • OR Python 3.12+ and pip (for local development)
  • Git (for GitOps functionality)

docs.title: Docker Compose (Recommended)
docs.text: The easiest way to get started with Easy IDP is using Docker Compose.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/BuckinghamIO/easy-idp.git
cd easy-idp

docs.title: 2. Configure Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file from the example:

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and set your credentials:

SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key-here
ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
ADMIN_PASSWORD=your-secure-password

Security

Make sure to change the default admin password before deploying to production!

docs.title: 3. Start Easy IDP
docs.text: docker-compose up -d

docs.title: 4. Access the Application
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to:

http://localhost:8000

Login with your admin credentials.

Installation Complete

You're now ready to create your first workflow! Continue to the Quickstart Guide.

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text: For local development or testing, you can run Easy IDP directly with Python.

docs.title: 1. Clone and Install Dependencies
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/BuckinghamIO/easy-idp.git
cd easy-idp
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: 2. Set Environment Variables
docs.text:
export SECRET_KEY="dev-secret-key"
export ADMIN_USERNAME="admin"
export ADMIN_PASSWORD="admin"

docs.title: 3. Run the Application
docs.text:
cd src
python app.py

The application will start on http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description SECRET_KEY dev-secret-key-change-in-production Flask secret key for session management ADMIN_USERNAME admin Admin username for initial login ADMIN_PASSWORD admin Admin password for initial login DB_PATH idp.db SQLite database file path

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: After installation, verify that Easy IDP is running correctly:

docs.title: 1. Check the Health Endpoint
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8000/

You should see the login page HTML.

docs.title: 2. Login to the Admin Panel
docs.text:
1. Navigate to http://localhost:8000
  2. Login with your admin credentials
  3. You should see the dashboard

docs.title: 3. Check the Database
docs.text:
The SQLite database should be created:

ls -lh database/idp.db

docs.title: Port Already in Use
docs.text:
If port 8000 is already in use, modify docker-compose.yml:

ports:
  - "8080:8000"  # Change host port to 8080

docs.title: Permission Issues
docs.text:
If you encounter permission issues with the database:

# Create database directory
mkdir -p database
chmod 755 database

docs.title: Docker Issues
docs.text:
If Docker containers won't start:

# Check Docker logs
docker-compose logs

# Rebuild containers
docker-compose down
docker-compose up --build

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
To upgrade Easy IDP to a new version:

# Pull latest changes
cd easy-idp
git pull

# Rebuild and restart
docker-compose down
docker-compose up --build -d

Database Backups

Always backup your database before upgrading: 

cp database/idp.db database/idp.db.backup

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide will walk you through creating and executing your first workflow in Easy IDP.

docs.title: Step 1: Login
docs.text:
Navigate to your Easy IDP instance and login with your admin credentials:

http://localhost:8000

docs.title: Step 2: View Available Workflows
docs.text:
After logging in, you'll see the Workflows page listing all available workflows.

For this quickstart, we'll use the example "Deploy Service" workflow that comes pre-configured.

docs.title: Step 3: Execute a Workflow
docs.text:
1. Click on "Deploy Service" workflow
  2. Fill out the form:
  3. Service Name: my-api
  4. Repository URL: https://github.com/your-org/my-api

  5. Environment: development

  6. Click "Execute Workflow"

docs.title: Step 4: Monitor Execution
docs.text:
You'll be redirected to the execution page where you can see:

  • ✅ Real-time step execution
  • 📋 Detailed logs for each step
  • ⏱️ Execution time and status
  • ⚠️ Any errors or warnings

The workflow will execute each step sequentially:

Step 1: Validate repository access ✓
Step 2: Create deployment configuration ✓
Step 3: Deploy to cluster ✓
Step 4: Verify deployment ✓

docs.title: Step 5: View Results
docs.text:
Once complete, you can:

  • View the full execution log
  • See output variables from each step
  • Download logs for auditing
  • Re-run the workflow if needed

docs.title: Create Your First Workflow
docs.text: Now let's create a simple custom workflow from scratch.

docs.title: Navigate to Admin Panel
docs.text: Click Admin → Workflows in the navigation bar.

docs.title: Create New Workflow
docs.text:
Click "New Workflow" and fill out the form:

Basic Information: 

Name: Hello World
Description: A simple test workflow
Version: 1.0

Form Schema: 

{
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "message",
      "label": "Message",
      "type": "text",
      "required": true,
      "default": "Hello, World!"
    }
  ]
}

Workflow Steps: 

[
  {
    "name": "Print Message",
    "action": "shell.exec",
    "params": {
      "command": "echo",
      "args": ["{{ inputs.message }}"]
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Save and Test
docs.text:
1. Click "Save Workflow"
  2. Navigate back to Workflows
  3. Find your "Hello World" workflow
  4. Click to execute it
  5. Enter a message and click "Execute"

You should see your message printed in the logs! 🎉

docs.title: Common Actions
docs.text:
HTTP Request: 

{
  "action": "http.request",
  "params": {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.example.com/deploy",
    "body": {"service": "{{ inputs.service_name }}"}
  }
}

Shell Command: 

{
  "action": "shell.exec",
  "params": {
    "command": "kubectl",
    "args": ["apply", "-f", "{{ vars.manifest_file }}"]
  }
}

Template Rendering: 

{
  "action": "template.render",
  "params": {
    "template": "k8s-deployment.yaml.j2",
    "output": "/tmp/deployment.yaml",
    "context": {"service": "{{ inputs.service_name }}"}
  }
}

docs.title: Variable Substitution
docs.text:
Access data in your workflows using template syntax:

  • {{ inputs.field_name }} - User input from form
  • {{ vars.variable_name }} - Variables set by previous steps
  • {{ globals.config_key }} - Global configuration values
  • {{ creds.alias.key }} - Credential values
  • {{ outputs.step_name.key }} - Output from previous step

docs.title: Workflow Fails to Execute
docs.text:
Check the logs for specific error messages. Common issues:

  • Missing required credentials
  • Invalid template syntax
  • Command not in allowlist

docs.title: Form Doesn't Validate
docs.text: Ensure your form schema is valid JSON and includes required fields.

docs.title: Can't See Workflow
docs.text:
Make sure you're logged in as admin or have the developer role.

Ready to build something more complex? Check out the Creating Workflows guide!

docs.title: Schema Reference
docs.text: Easy IDP uses YAML resources with JSON Schema validation to define your platform configuration. This approach provides strong typing, IDE support, and clear versioning.

docs.title: 📋 Available Resources
docs.text: Resource Description Schema Service Services, libraries, tools, and infrastructure components View Schema Team Team definitions with members and contacts View Schema Workflow Automated workflows and actions View Schema Scorecard Quality metrics and service maturity evaluation View Schema

docs.title: 🏗️ Resource Structure
docs.text:
All resources follow the same pattern:

apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1  # API version
kind: Service                      # Resource type

metadata:
  name: my-resource               # Unique identifier
  namespace: default              # Optional: namespace
  labels:                         # Key-value labels
    env: production
  annotations:                    # Non-identifying metadata
    docs: https://example.com

spec:
  # Resource-specific configuration
  type: service
  description: My service description
  # ... more fields

docs.title: API Version
docs.text:
apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1
  • Defines which schema version to use
  • Allows backward-compatible evolution
  • Current version: v1

docs.title: Kind
docs.text:
kind: Service
  • Resource type: Service, Team, Workflow, Scorecard
  • Determines which schema to validate against

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Common across all resources:

  • name: Unique identifier (lowercase-with-hyphens)
  • namespace: Logical grouping (optional, default: default)
  • labels: Key-value pairs for filtering and selection
  • annotations: Additional metadata (not used for selection)

docs.title: Spec
docs.text:
Resource-specific configuration. Each resource type has different fields:

  • Service: type, teams, repository, dependencies, etc.
  • Team: displayName, members, contacts, etc.
  • Workflow: parameters, steps, etc.
  • Scorecard: checks, scoring, etc.

docs.title: Option 1: Individual Files (Recommended)
docs.text:
platform-config/
├── services/
│   ├── payment-api.yaml
│   ├── user-service.yaml
│   └── auth-api.yaml
├── teams/
│   ├── platform-team.yaml
│   └── payment-team.yaml
└── workflows/
    └── deploy-service.yaml

Benefits: - Clear ownership (CODEOWNERS) - No merge conflicts - Easy to find specific resources

docs.title: Option 2: Multi-Document Files
docs.text:
# services/payment-system.yaml
---
apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payment-api
---
apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payment-worker
---
apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payment-db

Benefits: - Logically related resources together - Atomic changes (all-or-nothing) - Copy-paste friendly

docs.title: VSCode
docs.text:
Add to .vscode/settings.json:

{
  "yaml.schemas": {
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/service.schema.json": "services/*.yaml",
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/team.schema.json": "teams/*.yaml",
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/workflow.schema.json": "workflows/*.yaml",
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/scorecard.schema.json": "scorecards/*.yaml"
  }
}

Or use inline comments:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/service.schema.json
---
apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1
kind: Service
# ... VSCode now provides autocomplete and validation!

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Autocomplete: Suggest valid fields as you type
  • ✅ Validation: Real-time error checking
  • ✅ Documentation: Hover over fields for descriptions
  • ✅ Enum values: Show available options for choice fields

docs.title: 🔄 Versioning
docs.text:
Schemas use semantic versioning:

  • v1: Current stable version
  • v2: Next major version (breaking changes)
  • v1.1: Minor updates (backward compatible)

See Versioning for details on our stability promises.

docs.title: Service Schema
docs.text: Services are the core resource in Easy IDP. They represent any software component in your organization: APIs, libraries, tools, databases, websites, and infrastructure.

docs.title: Schema URL
docs.text: https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/service.schema.json

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/service.schema.json
---
apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1
kind: Service

metadata:
  name: payment-api
  labels:
    env: production

spec:
  type: service
  description: Payment processing API
  teams:
    - payment-team
  lifecycle: production
  repository:
    url: https://github.com/company/payment-api

docs.title: metadata.name (required)
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Pattern: ^[a-z0-9-]+$ (lowercase, hyphens only)
  • Length: 1-63 characters
  • Description: Unique service identifier

Examples: 

name: payment-api        ✅
name: user-service       ✅
name: PaymentAPI         ❌ (no uppercase)
name: payment_api        ❌ (no underscores)

docs.title: metadata.namespace
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Default: default
  • Description: Logical namespace for grouping services

Examples: 

namespace: default       # Default namespace
namespace: production    # Production services
namespace: experimental  # Experimental services

docs.title: metadata.labels
docs.text:
• Type: object
  • Description: Key-value pairs for filtering and selection

Examples: 

labels:
  env: production
  criticality: high
  language: python
  team: payment

docs.title: metadata.annotations
docs.text:
• Type: object
  • Description: Non-identifying metadata (not used for queries)

Examples: 

annotations:
  docs.url: https://docs.company.com/payment-api
  oncall.rotation: weekly
  cost.center: engineering

docs.title: spec.type (required)
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Allowed values:
  • service - Backend/API service
  • library - Shared library or package
  • tool - CLI tool or utility
  • website - Frontend website/webapp
  • infrastructure - Infrastructure component
  • database - Database
  • cache - Cache (Redis, Memcached)

Examples: 

type: service        # REST API, gRPC service
type: library        # npm package, Python library
type: website        # React app, marketing site
type: database       # PostgreSQL, MongoDB

docs.title: spec.description
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Max length: 500 characters
  • Description: Brief service description

Examples: 

description: Payment processing API with Stripe integration
description: User authentication and authorization service
description: Redis cache for session storage

docs.title: spec.owner
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Description: GitHub organization or username

Examples: 

owner: CompanyName
owner: PlatformTeam
owner: john-doe

docs.title: spec.teams (Multi-team ownership)
docs.text:
• Type: array of string
  • Min items: 1
  • Description: Teams that own/support this service

Examples: 

# Single team
teams:
  - platform-team

# Multi-team (shared ownership)
teams:
  - platform-team    # Primary
  - data-team        # Analytics access
  - security-team    # Security reviews

docs.title: spec.primaryTeam
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Description: Primary team for on-call (defaults to first in teams)

Examples: 

teams:
  - platform-team
  - data-team
primaryTeam: platform-team  # On-call responsibility

docs.title: spec.lifecycle
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Default: development
  • Allowed values:
  • development - In development
  • staging - Staging environment
  • production - Production
  • deprecated - Being phased out

Examples: 

lifecycle: production      # Live service
lifecycle: development     # WIP
lifecycle: deprecated      # Legacy system

docs.title: spec.repository
docs.text:
• Type: object
  • Description: Source code repository information

Fields:

  • url (string, required): Git repository URL
  • defaultBranch (string, default: main): Main branch name
  • private (boolean, default: false): Whether repo is private

Examples: 

repository:
  url: https://github.com/company/payment-api
  defaultBranch: main
  private: true

docs.title: spec.dependsOn
docs.text:
• Type: array of objects
  • Description: Dependencies on other resources

Each dependency:

  • kind (string, required): Resource type
  • name (string, required): Resource name
  • namespace (string, optional): Resource namespace

Examples: 

dependsOn:
  - kind: Service
    name: postgres-primary
  - kind: Service
    name: redis-cache
  - kind: Service
    name: auth-service
    namespace: security

docs.title: spec.links
docs.text:
• Type: object
  • Description: Links to external resources

Common links: - dashboard - Monitoring dashboard (Grafana, Datadog) - docs - Documentation - runbook - Runbook/playbook - logs - Log viewer - slack - Team Slack channel - repository - Source code - metrics - Metrics dashboard

Examples: 

links:
  dashboard: https://grafana.company.com/d/payment-api
  docs: https://docs.company.com/payment-api
  runbook: https://wiki.company.com/runbooks/payment-api
  logs: https://logs.company.com/payment-api
  slack: "#team-payment"
  metrics: https://datadog.company.com/dashboard/payment-api

docs.title: spec.tags
docs.text:
• Type: array of string
  • Description: Searchable tags/keywords

Examples: 

tags:
  - api
  - payment
  - stripe
  - pci-compliant
  - microservice

docs.title: spec.language
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Description: Primary programming language

Examples: 

language: Python
language: TypeScript
language: Go

docs.title: spec.framework
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Description: Primary framework

Examples: 

framework: FastAPI
framework: React
framework: Express

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/service.schema.json
---
apiVersion: idp.buckingham.io/v1
kind: Service

metadata:
  name: payment-api
  namespace: default
  labels:
    env: production
    criticality: high
    language: python
    team: payment
  annotations:
    docs.url: https://docs.company.com/payment-api
    oncall.rotation: weekly
    cost.center: engineering

spec:
  # Core info
  type: service
  description: Payment processing API with Stripe integration

  # Ownership (multi-team)
  owner: PaymentTeam
  teams:
    - payment-team      # Primary owner
    - platform-team     # Platform support
    - data-team         # Analytics access
  primaryTeam: payment-team  # On-call responsibility

  # Lifecycle
  lifecycle: production

  # Source code
  repository:
    url: https://github.com/company/payment-api
    defaultBranch: main
    private: true

  # Dependencies
  dependsOn:
    - kind: Service
      name: postgres-primary
    - kind: Service
      name: redis-cache
    - kind: Service
      name: auth-service

  # Links
  links:
    dashboard: https://grafana.company.com/d/payment-api
    docs: https://docs.company.com/payment-api
    runbook: https://wiki.company.com/runbooks/payment-api
    logs: https://logs.company.com/payment-api
    slack: "#team-payment"
    repository: https://github.com/company/payment-api
    metrics: https://datadog.company.com/dashboard/payment-api

  # Metadata
  tags:
    - api
    - payment
    - stripe
    - pci-compliant
  language: Python
  framework: FastAPI

docs.title: Multi-Team Services
docs.text:
Services can be owned by multiple teams:

spec:
  # Shared database example
  teams:
    - user-platform    # Primary owner
    - infra-data       # Infrastructure support
  primaryTeam: user-platform  # Responsible for on-call

Use cases: - Shared infrastructure (databases, caches) - Cross-functional services - Platform components with multiple stakeholders

The primary team handles: - On-call rotations - Incident response - Production changes

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
The schema allows additionalProperties: true in spec, enabling custom fields:

spec:
  # Standard fields
  type: service
  teams: [payment-team]

  # Custom extensions
  slos:
    availability: 99.9%
    latency_p95: 200ms

  cost:
    monthly_budget: 5000
    alerts_threshold: 6000

  compliance:
    pci_dss: true
    sox: true

  name: my-service

docs.title: VSCode Configuration
docs.text:
Add to your .vscode/settings.json:

{
  "yaml.schemas": {
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/service.schema.json": "services/*.yaml",
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/team.schema.json": "teams/*.yaml",
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/workflow.schema.json": "workflows/*.yaml",
    "https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/scorecard.schema.json": "scorecards/*.yaml"
  }
}

This enables: - ✅ Auto-completion - ✅ Inline documentation - ✅ Real-time validation - ✅ Error highlighting

docs.title: 📚 Documentation
docs.text: Full documentation available at: https://buckinghamio.github.io/easy-idp-docs/

docs.title: Semantic Versioning
docs.text:
Schemas follow semantic versioning:

  • Major version (v1 → v2): Breaking changes
  • Field removals
  • Type changes

  • Required field additions

  • Minor version (v1.0 → v1.1): Backward-compatible additions

  • New optional fields
  • New enum values

  • Relaxed constraints

  • Patch version (v1.0.0 → v1.0.1): Documentation fixes

  • No schema changes

docs.title: Stability Promise
docs.text:
• Schema URLs are permanent and will never return 404
  • Major versions supported for 1 year after next version release
  • 6 months deprecation notice before breaking changes
  • Migration guides provided for all major version upgrades

docs.title: 🤝 Contributing
docs.text: Found a bug or have a suggestion? Please open an issue or PR at: https://github.com/BuckinghamIO/easy-idp-docs

docs.title: Schema Change Guidelines
docs.text:
When proposing schema changes:

  1. Backward compatible (minor version):
  2. ✅ Add optional fields
  3. ✅ Add enum values

  4. ✅ Relax constraints

  5. Breaking changes (major version):

  6. ⚠️ Remove fields
  7. ⚠️ Change field types
  8. ⚠️ Make optional fields required
  9. ⚠️ Stricter validation

docs.title: Schema Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to Easy IDP schemas will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and schemas adhere to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Service Schema
docs.text:
• Initial release
  • Support for apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec structure
  • Metadata: name, namespace, labels, annotations
  • Spec fields:
  • type (service, library, tool, website, infrastructure, database, cache)
  • description
  • owner
  • teams (array for multi-team ownership)
  • primaryTeam (designated on-call owner)
  • lifecycle (development, staging, production, deprecated)
  • repository (url, defaultBranch, private)
  • dependsOn (array of resource dependencies)
  • links (dashboard, docs, runbook, etc.)
  • tags (searchable keywords)
  • language, framework

docs.title: Team Schema
docs.text:
• Initial release
  • Metadata: name, labels, annotations
  • Spec fields:
  • displayName
  • description
  • members (array with username, role, since)
  • contacts (slack, email, pagerduty)
  • links (wiki, jira, calendar, etc.)

docs.title: Workflow Schema
docs.text:
• Initial release
  • Metadata: name, labels, annotations
  • Spec fields:
  • displayName
  • description
  • parameters (input parameters with types)
  • steps (workflow execution steps)
  • tags

docs.title: Scorecard Schema
docs.text:
• Initial release
  • Metadata: name, labels, annotations
  • Spec fields:
  • displayName
  • description
  • appliesTo (resource selectors)
  • checks (evaluation rules)
  • scoring (levels: gold, silver, bronze)

docs.title: Schema Stability
docs.text:
• All fields marked as required in v1 will remain required in future v1.x versions
  • New optional fields may be added in v1.x (backward compatible)
  • Field removals or type changes require a new major version (v2)
  • additionalProperties: true in spec allows for custom extensions

docs.title: Planned for v2 (TBD)
docs.text:
• Enhanced dependency modeling (version constraints, optional vs required)
  • Service level objectives (SLOs) as first-class schema fields
  • Resource quotas and limits
  • API contract references (OpenAPI, GraphQL schemas)
  • Cost tracking metadata

docs.title: Deprecation Policy
docs.text:
• Major versions (v1, v2) supported for minimum 1 year after next version release
  • Deprecation warnings added 6 months before removal
  • Migration guides provided for all breaking changes
  • Old schema URLs remain accessible (never 404)

docs.title: Schema URLs
docs.text:
All schemas are available at stable URLs:

  • Service: https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/service.schema.json
  • Team: https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/team.schema.json
  • Workflow: https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/workflow.schema.json
  • Scorecard: https://schemas.easy-idp.com/v1/scorecard.schema.json

These URLs will never change or return 404 errors.

docs.title: Action Primitives
docs.text: Easy IDP provides a set of powerful action primitives that can be composed to create complex workflows.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Actions are the building blocks of workflows. Each action performs a specific task such as making an HTTP request, executing a shell command, or rendering a template.

docs.title: http.request
docs.text:
Make HTTP/HTTPS requests to external APIs or services.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description method string Yes HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.) url string Yes Full URL to request headers object No HTTP headers body object/string No Request body timeout int No Request timeout in seconds (default: 30)

Example:

{
  "name": "Create GitHub Repository",
  "action": "http.request",
  "params": {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.github.com/orgs/{{ globals.github_org }}/repos",
    "headers": {
      "Authorization": "Bearer {{ creds.github.token }}",
      "Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"
    },
    "body": {
      "name": "{{ inputs.repo_name }}",
      "private": true,
      "auto_init": true
    }
  }
}

Output:

{
  "status_code": 201,
  "body": {...},
  "headers": {...}
}

docs.title: shell.exec
docs.text:
Execute shell commands on the server.

Security

Commands must be in the allowlist for security. Contact your administrator to add new commands.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description command string Yes Command to execute args array No Command arguments cwd string No Working directory env object No Environment variables

Example:

{
  "name": "Deploy to Kubernetes",
  "action": "shell.exec",
  "params": {
    "command": "kubectl",
    "args": [
      "apply",
      "-f",
      "{{ vars.manifest_path }}",
      "-n",
      "{{ inputs.namespace }}"
    ],
    "env": {
      "KUBECONFIG": "/etc/kubernetes/config"
    }
  }
}

Output:

{
  "exit_code": 0,
  "stdout": "deployment.apps/my-service created",
  "stderr": ""
}

docs.title: template.render
docs.text:
Render Jinja2 templates to files.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description template string Yes Template file name output string Yes Output file path context object Yes Template variables

Example:

{
  "name": "Generate Kubernetes Manifest",
  "action": "template.render",
  "params": {
    "template": "k8s-deployment.yaml.j2",
    "output": "/tmp/deployment.yaml",
    "context": {
      "service_name": "{{ inputs.service_name }}",
      "image": "{{ inputs.image }}",
      "replicas": "{{ inputs.replicas }}"
    }
  }
}

Template Example (templates/k8s-deployment.yaml.j2):

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ service_name }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ replicas }}
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: {{ service_name }}
        image: {{ image }}

Output:

{
  "output_path": "/tmp/deployment.yaml",
  "size_bytes": 512
}

docs.title: flow.set_vars
docs.text:
Set or derive variables for use in subsequent steps.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description vars object Yes Variables to set (key-value pairs)

Example:

{
  "name": "Set Derived Variables",
  "action": "flow.set_vars",
  "params": {
    "vars": {
      "full_service_name": "{{ inputs.environment }}-{{ inputs.service_name }}",
      "manifest_path": "/tmp/{{ inputs.service_name }}-deployment.yaml",
      "timestamp": "{{ now() | datetime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S') }}"
    }
  }
}

Output:

{
  "vars_set": ["full_service_name", "manifest_path", "timestamp"]
}

docs.title: flow.assert
docs.text:
Assert conditions with fail-fast behavior.

Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description condition string Yes Boolean expression to evaluate error_message string No Custom error message on failure

Example:

{
  "name": "Validate Service Name",
  "action": "flow.assert",
  "params": {
    "condition": "{{ inputs.service_name | regex_match('^[a-z0-9-]+$') }}",
    "error_message": "Service name must be lowercase alphanumeric with dashes"
  }
}

Output:

{
  "passed": true
}

docs.title: Variable Substitution
docs.text: All action parameters support template variable substitution using Jinja2 syntax.

docs.title: Available Variables
docs.text:
inputs - User input from workflow form: 

{{ inputs.service_name }}
{{ inputs.environment }}

vars - Variables set by flow.set_vars: 

{{ vars.full_service_name }}
{{ vars.timestamp }}

globals - Global configuration values: 

{{ globals.github_org }}
{{ globals.cluster_domain }}

creds - Credential values: 

{{ creds.github.token }}
{{ creds.aws.access_key }}

outputs - Output from previous steps: 

{{ outputs.create_repo.body.id }}
{{ outputs.deploy.exit_code }}

docs.title: Jinja2 Filters
docs.text:
String manipulation: 

{{ inputs.name | upper }}
{{ inputs.name | lower }}
{{ inputs.name | title }}
{{ inputs.name | replace(' ', '-') }}

Regex: 

{{ inputs.email | regex_match('.*@example\\.com') }}
{{ inputs.version | regex_search('\\d+\\.\\d+') }}

JSON: 

{{ outputs.api_call.body | tojson }}
{{ vars.data | fromjson }}

Date/Time: 

{{ now() }}
{{ now() | datetime('%Y-%m-%d') }}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All actions return a status indicating success or failure. If an action fails:

  1. Workflow execution stops immediately
  2. Error details are logged
  3. Workflow status set to "failed"
  4. User is notified

Example error output:

{
  "error": "Command 'kubectl' returned non-zero exit code 1",
  "details": {
    "exit_code": 1,
    "stderr": "Error: deployment not found"
  }
}

docs.title: 1. Use Meaningful Step Names
docs.text:
// ❌ Bad
{"name": "Step 1", "action": "http.request", ...}

// ✅ Good
{"name": "Create GitHub Repository", "action": "http.request", ...}

docs.title: 2. Validate Input Early
docs.text:
// Add validation steps at the beginning
{
  "name": "Validate Service Name",
  "action": "flow.assert",
  "params": {
    "condition": "{{ inputs.service_name | length > 0 }}"
  }
}

docs.title: 3. Set Intermediate Variables
docs.text:
// Instead of complex nested templates
{
  "name": "Prepare Variables",
  "action": "flow.set_vars",
  "params": {
    "vars": {
      "repo_url": "https://github.com/{{ globals.github_org }}/{{ inputs.repo_name }}"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 4. Use Descriptive Error Messages
docs.text:
{
  "name": "Check Cluster Access",
  "action": "flow.assert",
  "params": {
    "condition": "{{ creds.kubernetes.token | length > 0 }}",
    "error_message": "Kubernetes credentials not configured. Please set up credentials in Admin panel."
  }
}
